question: In what sense is the Self described as the dancer of the cosmic drama?
premises: The Self, grounded in its own hidden nature, unfolds the manifold roles of waking, dream, and deep sleep through the play of its powers.
This unfolding occurs on the wall of consciousness alone, without any external material cause, by the Self's own vibration.
Scriptural authorities identify this same Self as the inner self in bondage and as the sole supreme Lord who initiates, sustains, and withdraws the world-drama.
inference: Therefore the Self is the cosmic dancer who freely manifests, enacts, and reabsorbs the entire drama of the universe within consciousness.
plain_english: The Self is called a dancer because it brings forth the whole play of waking, dream, and deep sleep from within its own hidden nature. It does this on the screen of consciousness alone, by the spontaneous play of its powers, without needing any outside material. The same Self appears as the inner individual bound by impressions, yet it remains the one supreme Lord who alone can begin, sustain, and end the drama of the three worlds.
